sources.news_title: Train carrying ethanol derailed near Lancing in Morgan County
TEMA assisting Morgan County after train derailment, evacuation center open for those impacted
sources.text:
UPDATE: Morgan County officials say response and cleanup efforts are continuing following the Norfolk Southern train derailment on Thursday, June 11, in the Lancing, Tennessee area.
As of 10:00am Friday, emergency management officials said the fire at the derailment site remains active, with crews continuing to work in the remote area. Limited access to the site has made response and cleanup operations more challenging.
Officials said overnight air monitoring conducted by Norfolk Southern contractors found no issues. Personnel from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation remain on site to monitor conditions and support air quality testing. Authorities said there is currently no threat to the public.
Cleanup operations have begun in phases after the National Transportation Safety Board reviewed footage and approved removal efforts for some train cars. Officials said not all cars will be cleared immediately, and cleanup could take several days or up to a week to complete.
Residents may encounter intermittent road closures as heavy equipment is transported to and from the site. Officials are asking the public to avoid the area and follow local guidance.
The evacuation center previously established at Central High School has been closed after no residents sought shelter there.
Morgan County Emergency Management said additional updates will be provided as cleanup efforts continue.
PREVIOUS STORY: The Tennessee Emergency Management Agency (TEMA) is assisting Morgan County officials following a train derailment in the county on Thursday afternoon.
According to TEMA, a district coordinator has been deployed to the scene at Morgan County's request to support local response efforts.
Morgan County officials have opened an evacuation center at Central High School for residents impacted by the incident. Emergency officials are urging residents to follow local guidance, stay updated through official Morgan County channels, and avoid the affected area so crews can safely respond.
No additional details about the derailment or any injuries have been released.

Evacuations ordered after train derailment in rural Tennessee
sources.text:
US News
Evacuations ordered after train derailment in rural Tennessee
Evacuations have been ordered in part of Morgan County, Tennessee, after several train cars carrying ethanol derailed in a rural area and sparked a fire, according to local officials and media reports. No injuries have been reported.
The derailment happened in the Lancing area, according to Morgan County E-911, which said emergency crews were on scene and evaluating the situation. The Tennessee Emergency Management Agency (TEMA) said it was supporting county officials and had a district coordinator at the scene.
Morgan County officials ordered evacuations for several nearby roads as a precaution, including parts of Emory Heights, Homestead, Broken Antler, Lazy Bear, Shady Grove and Thomas Drive.
An evacuation center has been opened at Central High School, according to TEMA. Residents were told to follow local guidance, monitor updates from Morgan County officials and avoid the affected area so emergency crews can respond safely.
A Norfolk Southern representative told WVLT that the train was carrying ethanol but said there was no danger to the public. Morgan County Sheriff Rick Hamby told the station that the rural location was making the response difficult, including access to the derailment site.
Officials believe four or five train cars derailed. No injuries have been reported.

sources.news_title: Train carrying ethanol derails in Morgan County
sources.text:
A Norfolk Southern train derailed in Morgan County near milepost 243.9 on Thursday around 3:23 p.m. Norfolk Southern Media Relations said the train contained ethanol, but there was no danger to the public.
“While it is a very remote location, out of an abundance of caution, emergency responders are evacuating local residents near the area,” Norfolk Southern said. “There is no impact to local road traffic. The nearest crossing is approximately two miles from the site.”
No injuries were reported. Norfolk Southern said it was still working to determine the number of train cars involved.
“Norfolk Southern teams are on site with additional response crews en route,” Norfolk Southern said. “We’re coordinating with the Morgan County Sheriff’s Office and other local authorities and first responders.”

sources.news_title: Sheriff's Office: Evacuation notice issued after train derailment in Morgan County
Evacuation order lifted following train derailment in Morgan County
sources.text:
Evacuation order lifted following train derailment in Morgan County
According officials, 15 to 20 cars derailed and four or five of them contained ethanol.
MORGAN COUNTY, Tenn. (WVLT) - Emergency officials lifted an hours-long evacuation order in Morgan County Thursday night after a Norfolk Southern train carrying ethanol derailed near Lansing.
According to first responders on the scene, between 15 and 20 cars derailed. Several of those cars, four or five according to responders, were carrying ethanol.
An update from Norfolk Southern said no one was injured in the crash.
Related Coverage: Norfolk Southern’s ‘Safety Train’ makes a stop in Knoxville
County officials said Tennessee EMA has district coordinators on scene and the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation had deployed air monitoring crews to help with the response.
Additionally, the National Park Service is asking visitors to Obed Wild and Scenic River to stay out of the park’s water.
It marks the fifth Tennessee train derailment in 2026, according to the U.S. Federal Rail Association.

sources.news_title: Train derails in Morgan County, officials say
Train derailment in Morgan County prompts emergency response
sources.text:
Train derailment in Morgan County prompts emergency response
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WZTV) — Emergency officials have ordered evacuations in parts of Morgan County after a train derailment Thursday prompted a large-scale response from local and state agencies.
The Tennessee Emergency Management Agency said it is assisting Morgan County officials following the derailment. A TEMA district coordinator is at the scene to support the incident as well.
Emergency responders remain on scene in the Lancing area and are evaluating conditions, according to Morgan County E-911.
As a precaution, officials have ordered evacuations in several nearby areas, including:
- Emory Heights (125-993)
- Homestead (126-598)
- Broken Antler (262-430)
- Lazy Bear (308-441)
- Shady Grove (920-1075)
- Thomas Drive (215-772)
Officials said those are the areas currently subject to evacuation orders and noted that additional updates will be provided as information becomes available.
Morgan County has established an evacuation center at Central High School for residents impacted by the incident.
Authorities are urging residents to follow instructions from local officials, monitor emergency updates, and avoid the affected area to allow first responders to safely conduct their work.
As of 5:45 p.m., officials have not yet released additional details about the cause of the derailment or whether any injuries have been reported.
This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

sources.news_title: NTSB Sending Team to East Tennessee to Investigate Yesterday’s Norfolk Southern Derailment
sources.text:
NTSB Sending Team to East Tennessee to Investigate Yesterday’s Norfolk Southern Derailment
Written by David C. Lester, Editor-in-ChiefATLANTA –– On Thursday, June 11, a Norfolk Southern train derailed near Wartburg, Tenn., which is just west of Knoxville.
The NTSB says that 26 cars were involved, and County officials said about 4 or 5 cars had caught fire. There were no injuries, but the incident prompted officials to evacuate residents within one square mile of the site, which involved 12 homes. However, the evacuation order was lifted at around 9:00 p.m.
The NTSB announced early Friday morning that it was sending an investigation team to the derailment site: “NTSB is sending a team to investigate the June 11, 2026, Norfolk Southern freight train derailment near Wartburg, Tennessee. Approximately 26 rail cars were involved, including ethanol tank cars. Several cars were breached, resulting in a fire.”
RT&S will continue to monitor this story.
